subject: Edge VPC zoning, Terraform module alignment & CI gating — final review
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, engops@edgecloud.io
Cc: hiro.tanaka@redwood.com, infra@acme.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge VPC zoning, Terraform module alignment & CI gating — final review

Team / EdgeCloud —

Thanks for the patience on this final pass. Attached is the updated VPC zoning diagram (vpc-zoning-diagram-20260401.png) and a trimmed patch that consolidates our Terraform module boundaries (tf-modules-edgecloud-diff.patch). The goal for this thread is narrow: call out any remaining blockers for the private deployment IaC set (Terraform + Helm + Ansible), confirm CI gating steps, and lock a sign-off timeline so the infra schedule (ACME kickoff 2026-04-12) stays intact.

Open items I want us to confirm here:
- Network zoning: management/control/data plane CIDR isolation and expected port lists (we proposed management in a /26; please flag if Acme needs larger).
- BGP / peering constraints: EdgeCloud has a BGP edge — need confirmation of route filtering and ASN agreement.
- Terraform modules split: we proposed separate modules for vpc, routing, firewall, and private-endpoints (see patch). Are the exported variables and outputs stable for the operator?
- Helm release ordering + hooks for DB init and secrets; expect a post-install Ansible run for host-level config in on-prem racks.
- CI gating: terraform plan cannot be auto-applied without a two-person signoff; smoke tests must pass in staging (list in ci-gating-checklist-privdeploy.md).

Please reply with inline comments or a single consolidated approval by EOD Friday (2026-04-02 PST) if possible. If EdgeCloud or Acme Security need a separate Zoom with networking diagrams, say so and we will book.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

---

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, engops@edgecloud.io
Cc: hiro.tanaka@redwood.com, infra@acme.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge VPC zoning, Terraform module alignment & CI gating — final review

Monica — quick notes inline for visibility, posting as a single reply to keep thread tidy. I attached the trimmed plan outputs and a short checklist for terraform module compatibility (tf-modules-edgecloud-diff.patch contains comments). Attachments: tf-plan-summary.txt (snippet) referenced in the patch.

1) Network zoning
- Management plane /26 is fine for initial cluster (supports ~60 hosts). I'll add a variable so Acme can widen to /25 without module changes.
- Required ports: SSH from bastion (22), health-checking (8080/8443), kubelet (10250) locked to control plane. I'll produce a minimal iptables map for on-prem ops.

2) BGP
- EdgeCloud: need their allowed prefixes list. For now plan contains a max-prefix filter and community stripping. If Acme wants to advertise additional customer prefixes, they'll need to register ASN with EdgeCloud first.

3) Terraform modules
- Split looks correct. One note: the private-endpoints module currently exposes an endpoint resource name that the Helm chart expects; I added a stable output (private_endpoint_id) in the patch. Please confirm the Helm chart uses that output instead of a hardcoded name.

4) Helm + Ansible sequence
- Helm chart will be templated to wait on endpoint readiness (readiness probe). After successful helm upgrade, the Ansible playbook runs host-config (ntp, sysctl, container runtime tuning). I've added a hook to the chart that writes a /var/run/privdeploy-ready file; the playbook looks for that file.

5) CI gating
- Implementing: 1) terraform fmt & validate; 2) terraform plan posted to MR; 3) two approvers to allow apply in prod; 4) smoke test job in staging that hits the private endpoint via an envoy proxy in the VPC. The ci-gating-checklist doc enumerates exact jobs.

Blockers from my side: we need an explicit list of allowed egress destinations from Acme racks (for outbound telemetry and CVE patching). If security@acme can provide that this week, we can complete the firewall rules.

-Dev

---

From: EdgeCloud Solutions <engops@edgecloud.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: infra@acme.com, security@acme.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2026 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge VPC zoning, Terraform module alignment & CI gating — final review

Hi all — thanks for the detailed notes. A few clarifications from EdgeCloud ops: 

- BGP / ASN: We can peer on ASN 64512 for the initial setup. We'll send a csv of allowed prefixes for Acme by EOD Tuesday. We will also strip any BGP communities that match our internal tenancy tags; if Acme needs pass-through communities we'll need a policy exception.

- Route leak protection: our edge will reject any route advertisements with more-specific prefixes unless explicitly permitted. For simplicity we recommend Acme uses a /22 block for the customer-announced space; if they must keep smaller subnets we will add explicit allow-lists.

- NAT & Egress: For on-prem racks, we can provide a managed egress proxy (recommended) or allow direct outbound subject to ACLs. Managed proxy supports TLS termination and HTTP allow-lists — it's the easier compliance path.

- Terraform outputs: we prefer the private_endpoint_id be an explicit tag (name: acme-priv-endpoint-{{env}}) rather than an opaque ID to simplify the EdgeCloud provisioning step. The patch looks good but please add name tag in addition to ID output.

We'll do a short 30-minute sync on Wed 2026-04-07 at 09:00 PT if that works for Redwood + Acme Security.

Cheers,
EdgeCloud Ops

- Acme Security to share egress whitelist (target: 2026-04-06 EOD).
- EdgeCloud to share allowed prefixes csv and confirm 64512 peering (we have Wed 9am PT sync booked — calendar invite inbound).
- I will update the CI gating MR and add an explicit reviewers list (Priyom and Hiro as infra approvers).

If all targets are met we sign off on infra merge and schedule the on-prem deploy window for 2026-04-12 to 2026-04-14. Please react with "+1" if you accept the schedule.

Monica Patel
